claim.quote: we measured the scintillation from electronic recoils ranging between 36.3 and 185 keV$_\mathrm{ee}$, yielding a mean signal size of $1.25^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$~phe/keV$_\mathrm{ee}$, and nuclear recoils from 53.2 to 1090 keV$_\mathrm{nr}$.

name: Scintillation yield from electronic and nuclear recoils in superfluid $^4$He
notes: Collaboration tag on the paper is 'SPICE/HeRALD Collaboration'.

summary.plain: A 16 cm^3 sample of superfluid helium viewed by six photomultiplier tubes was used to measure how much light electron and nuclear recoils produce, which sets how well a helium dark matter detector can tell signal from background.
summary.technical: Scintillation yield of 1.75 K superfluid 4He for electronic recoils (36.3-185 keVee) and nuclear recoils (53.2-1090 keVnr) read out by six immersed PMTs, compared to a semiempirical model; delayed scintillation components studied as a handle on recoil-type discrimination.

title: Scintillation yield from electronic and nuclear recoils in superfluid $^4$He
why_it_matters: The abstract says the relative yields set the sensitivity and discrimination power of a superfluid 4He dark matter detector.
